rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two archive winners (TotalCorporateCashUses and RequirementWithSlowingInventoryTurns) with no new economic content, and it double-counts inventory (Δinvt inside the uses leg, invt/sale in the conditioner), so any gain over the existing t=−3.59 version would be uninterpretable and almost certainly within noise of the parent signals.

The proposal openly concedes it "isolates the measurement question rather than the economic one" — averaging two already-tested inventory conditioners (t=−4.25 and t=−3.59) into a SUMRANK is a cosmetic variant of both parents, and a composite of two correlated inventory ratios cannot discriminate the mechanism it claims to test.

This is the exact intersection of two existing archive signals — PeerRelativeFundingRequirement and TotalCorporateCashUses — differing only by the addition of the aqc term inside an already-tested IND_RANK, which is too trivial an increment to warrant a separate test; the industry-neutrality argument would have justified the peer-relative version, which has already been run.

The capex-stripping test is a legitimate discriminating experiment against the CMA/asset-growth (Cooper-Gulen-Schill) spanning concern that plausibly explains the whole capex-containing family, but the resulting expression is close to inventory growth interacted with inventory-turnover deterioration — i.e., near the published inventory-growth anomaly (Belo-Lin) — so a positive result should be read as mechanism identification rather than a new signal.

This is the most economically distinct proposal in the batch — the two legs share no inputs and it substitutes an operating-cost-rigidity conditioner for the archive's over-recycled oancf/lt ratio — though the reviewer should be prepared to attribute any result partly to the known standalone hiring-rate anomaly (Belo-Lin-Bazdresch) rather than to the conjunction.

Substituting ib for oancf to lift coverage from ~0.08 to ~0.12 is a defensible robustness test of the archive's binding sparse-sample weakness rather than a pure performance chase, but it remains a recombination of two existing signals and should be judged on whether the wide-sample result is comparable, not on whether it happens to score higher.
